limitations: The sampler is bound to resident logits and returns only a compact four-u32 result, but this standalone benchmark owns synthetic input logits.
The verifier-grade kernel performs repeated vocabulary scans for each top-k rank and is O(top_k * vocabulary); it is not the promoted bandwidth-limit design.
The engine supplies an explicit canonical draw. On-device deterministic RNG state is not implemented.
Timing uses host command submission/completion and no Metal hardware counters.
This evidence does not cover final recovered model quality, stochastic MTP acceptance, long-context residency, or a complete decoder token step.
conclusion: The resident bounded sampler is token-decision equivalent to the canonical Rust sampler and faster than the host reference on this synthetic full-vocabulary distribution. It remains a verifier candidate pending a bandwidth-efficient selection algorithm, on-device RNG, complete-graph integration evidence, and final-model golden gates.
